verdicts.title: Brains and pseudorandom generators
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In a pioneering classic, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts proposed a model of the central nervous system; motivated by EEG recordings of normal brain activity, Chv\' atal and Goldsmith asked whether or not this model can be engineered to provide pseudorandom number generators. We supply evidence suggesting that the answer is negative.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns a McCulloch-Pitts neural model and its capacity to produce pseudorandom generators, with no mention of Nisan-Wigderson designs, Zeckendorf representations, or Fourier/parity bias bounds.

verdicts.title: A note on closed-form representation of Fibonacci numbers using Fibonacci trees
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper, we give a new representation of the Fibonacci numbers. This is achieved using Fibonacci trees. With the help of this representation, the nth Fibonacci number can be calculated without having any knowledge about the previous Fibonacci numbers.

verdicts.title: Bounds on Zeckendorf Games
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Zeckendorf proved that every positive integer $n$ can be written uniquely as the sum of non-adjacent Fibonacci numbers.
